correctness.rationale: For fixed 0<p<r and ε>0, the C¹ increasing bijection z=sgn(x)log(1+|x|) exactly transforms xdot=(2sin t+εp)|x|+2sin t−ε(r−p) into zdot=2sin t+ε[p−r exp(−|z|)]. At ε=0 all solutions are s−2cos t. Integrating for one turn yields displacement εr(λ−J_ε(s)), λ=2πp/r; the uniform global bound |J_ε−I|≤(2π)² ε(p+r) excludes remote roots. The convolution I(s)=2∫_{−2}²exp(−|s−u|)/(4−u²)^{1/2}du is even and satisfies I−I=−4/(4−s²)^{1/2} on |s|<2. I0>2 is certified by the explicit elementary lower-integral bound. With h=I′, (h′sinh s−h cosh s)′=−4s sinh s/(4−s²)^{3/2}<0, giving one positive maximum at s* and the two/four/zero simple-root regimes. Uniform C¹ convergence of J_ε near simple roots also holds at grazing s=±2: |z_ε−(s−2cos t)|=O(ε), ∂_s z_ε=1+O(ε), and uniformly in s the set {|s−2cos t|≤Cε} has measure O(√ε), so the sign discontinuity in the derivative contributes o(1) even when the source text’s transverse-crossing simplification is inapplicable. Thus each simple root persists uniquely and no others appear for small ε. The derivative of the return map is 1−εr I′(s_j)+o(ε), giving alternating hyperbolic stability, and I(2)<2<I0 ensures all four in the middle regime cross zero. The two critical response levels are explicitly excluded.
residual_risks: Only sufficiently small ε>0 for fixed parameters away from λ=I0 and λ=I*; no critical-level or all-ε classification.

Neither implies four hyperbolic cycles with strictly first harmonic coefficients. No covering same-class Resultary finding located other than this assigned record.
